simple.meaning: מַלְבֵּן (malbên) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a brickkiln.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 2 Samuel 12:31. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַלְבֵּן (H4404) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מַלְבֵּן (malbên) / H4404 is traced through 2 Samuel 12:31, Jeremiah 43:9, Nahum 3:14 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He brought out the people who were in it, and put them under saws, under iron picks, under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brick kiln; and he did so to all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

definitions.full: H4404. malben מַלְבֵּן noun [masculine] 1 brick-mould ; 2 quadrangle (on meaning brick-mould , and figurative something rectangular , see Hoffm ZAW 1882, 53-72 Dr 2Sam 12:31 , compare Late Hebrew מַלְבֵּן ; Arabic ; Syriac ); — 1 brick-mould , 2Sam 12:31 Qr (Kt, by error, מלכן ), Nahum 3:14 . 2 quadrangle , Jer 43:9 (at Tahpanhes).
